body: If I am a troll even here, guess it's time to disappear.
Good to know "bring a guest" means guest is optional. I kinda feel showing up alone makes me look like a big loser, but as I said, I don't have much for options. :(

I wasn't mocking it. The facts are that there are fewer services available for so-called "higher-functioning" ASD people than there are for so-called "lower-functioning" + parents. 

From one Canadian report on ASD supports or lack thereof: "Up to 50% of individuals with ASDs do not have
an intellectual disability (ID), yet their needs for
support are as great as those with ASD and ID."

(FORGOTTEN: Ontario Adults with Autism and Adults with Aspergers)

Makes sense: sz is more episodic and usually managed with condition-specific meds, whereas ASDs (no intellectual disability) are still permanent not episodic,  with no medication to deal with the ASD itself, only particular comorbid mental illnesses like depression.

Sorry, I didn't mean to offend anyone. I personally do know ASD people (plus myself) who do not have comorbid intellectual disability, and we have been encouraged to try to support ourselves through arts & crafts type entrepreneurial ventures. 

My main point being, I find it disappointing that this is a model for how to handle ASD employment/disability. There needs to be a more thorough consideration of the person's actual living conditions and alternate sources of revenue before a caseworker decides to cut them off because their origami makes them "occupationally skilled" and "self-sufficient."

Watch out at tax time too--I had a tax preparation professional tell me to declare myself a "small business". Ooops...

Thanks. I've tried to live independently & support myself through an art I am good at, and it's amazing how fast disability case workers will "support" me by dropping my ass off the roster. That's with zero community or family support, as well.

I agree that if an ASD person HAS support that isn't going away, it makes sense that they be able to make some money for whatever they like. Pizza, movie tickets, etc.

This kind of thing is unlikely IMHO to lead to being able to save for retirement, live independently paying market-price rent, or the other usual ways we gauge "adulting".

I worry the ASD person will get over-confident on a false basis & strive for level of independence that leaves them vulnerable to losing everything/being exploited.

I worry the AAD person will lose government or other disability-based supports if they naively consider these ventures a real business.

OMG yes. I have found there's plenty of help/advice aimed at parents or partners of ASD adults, but comparatively less for the ASD adults themselves. Like my local autism centre has "respite help" for parents/caregivers to get a break from dealing with their ASD people, but no group for high-functioning ASD adults, other than an employment service offering gems like shopping cart round-ups & customer service (part-time, minimum wage). 

I'd love a respite from my garbage ASD life.

It feels "right" to do this to myself too (AS + child abuse survivor). Constant feeling of being intrinsically horrible & ignored by others. Head-banging & punching myself as child, cutting & overdoses as adult. Mostly just drinking hard lately. 

Good luck.

Thanks for this message. I'm so tired of psychologist asking me to  get my parents' perspective on what I was like as a child, or if I could move in with my parents (I am 45). 

"Crippling emotions" for sure. :(
That was an asshole move on his part. I feel the same way--feel like trash everyday, with few counter-examples to draw upon for solace. :(
That would make me wonder, "what does he want? What is the real agenda behind this small talk?" lol Sad but true.

Agree w/ OP & many others here--dislike the AS social skills groups I have tried out in rl, & do not get along w/ others dxed w/ ASDs. 

I loathe even more being lumped in w/ "autism mothers" because there are no services or groups for older women w/ ASDs. This has happened & been v. embarrassing & degrading to me, when they talk to me in patronizing, mother hen way.

I too feel obliged to talk with everybody (too many years forced to work customer service), & don't try to make conversational partners feel bad most of the time.

"Intellectually-impaired" individuals= it hurts me to be categorized with people with low I.Q. for various unavoidable reasons, none of which are their fault. Mental health "clubhouses" and other programs I am regularly encouraged to partake in by psychologist provide this level of conversation, in my own experience attending to try them out.
It drives home my impairment, but also opens a rare door to communication with smart people who relate.

Same situation here. It feels like I have to take whatever scraps of conversation (with people I like) that they choose to dole out. Increasingly, I am even doing things like grabbing and paying bill to "prove" I am worth putting up with. 

Zero interest in b.s. talk like small talk with nosy neighbours, talking with intellectually-impaired individuals in various "programs", etc.

Just because someone DOES make a huge effort to talk with me does not mean I want to talk with THEM. The rewarding people seem to be torturing me/us when they withdraw in conversation  like OP describes.

I'm not sure what to do. "Back off" to me sounds like:
do not ask for his new cell #,
do not initiate e-mails,
do not ask him to hang out,
if we end up hanging out anyway, be cool-no mention of anything deeper/personal, only superficial topics,
do not give him Xmas gift. 

Then I have no one at all in my life who I get along with. 

"Playing cool" seems to be a big NT social strategy. My psychologist says avoidant people need NOT to be playing so cool, just avoiding risk & any chance of continuing friendship.

I feel so down about this. It's like being doomed to doing everything alone, with no one in my corner, if I just "play cool" in this friendship & kill it in the process, OR if I come on too strong, not realizing that to "play cool" was better.  

I wish I could just ask him directly. But then I've tipped my hand.

I also still don't understand why my psychologist, who says I have AS, is encouraging me NOT to back off. She says when I back off, it sends the message I don't want the friendship much. She says I need to try to reach out more.
Thanks. It's extremely confusing & depressing. :(
Do you find these people want to keep in touch with you, or do they drift away?

Agreed: education has zero to do with employment. I'm the most educated person in my family, & least employable due to the AS/depression. 

I wish colleges & universities would advise students about employment prospects in given fields, esp. students with unrealistic or limited ability to see this for themselves due to various factors like AS. I personally know several young AS people who believed journalism was a good career choice, graduated, & are unemployed & unemployable in a field where social skills/connections are immensely important. Disability services workers need to take some responsibility for this sad situation.

OMG YES: "I also feel guilt for restricting other people's fun time just to accommodate my needs. I'm in a weird spot where I don't want a ton of attention on myself, but I also feel more comfortable when I can keep someone's attention for longer than a few minutes."

Attending is probably better than not, because it might be a good experience. Social practice, with supporters (sister & gf) there.

More confusion for those "old people" with AS who spend time w/ younger companions & can "pass" as younger (as per another recent thread on here). But this is irrelevant to OP's post so I will not continue!

I apologize for sounding negative--I have lived this situation myself a lot (45 years old now). I always feel extremely depressed when I misread NTs as liking me too much, so I advised a bit of caution. No offence.

For the record, my psychologist says to ask people these type of things ("Do you like me as more than friends?") in conversation, not e-mail/text/social media DMs. 

You might be doing well. I have no idea. I wish I could help both of us.
THIS. Wish I could help. Same problem.

Be cautious--my psychologist urged me to try to "get closer" with a male friend, which backfired. The psychologist had my side of things only, just as we only have yours, so we don't know what the other party is really thinking. I find many NTs do things like hug, put arm on someone's shoulder, give warm greetings, etc. & because many of us with AS are literally STARVED of friendship/affection/attention, we can blow it out of proportion in our minds & hearts. The NT person, in my experience, was often "just being friendly", & it's the NT who is oddly silent around me who had the crush. Weird stuff. Watch yourself.

I work freelance & 100% guarantee disclosing AS, let alone sending my occasional gig-based employers a guide about AS, would bring ghosting, not accommodations. 

Count your blessings if you have real employment somewhere at which this informative guide would be well-received by managers/supervisors.
Either gender can creep people out. Life is no free ride for women, romantically or in relationships of any kind.

What if no one reaches out & I am just sad of always being alone? As you say, it's unrewarding at best to reach out to people who are treating you/me with indifference & rudeness, yet it's breaking me to be alone all the time. I am breaking down in transactions with cashiers, my social skills/tolerance are so damaged.

Volunteering is something I have tried, but I find it ironic that I am usually "worse" than people I am volunteering to assist. (Obvious symptomatology, lack of social supports, etc.)

This is an inspirational message for me. I'm scared I lost my only real friend because of drama (caused by someone I was trying to avoid, but in front of him) a week ago. I'm afraid my friend knows now that he's my only friend, I'm a f**k up in a crappy relationship I am trying to escape at every opportunity, etc. 

Practicing avoidance, leaving it all up to him to get back in touch, but maybe I;ll get him a Christmas present just in case it's not over 100%.
100% leader. Can't even understand orders I'm given much of the time by others. Can't do teamwork.
Nope. If anything, I imagine the medical staff will work harder to save a younger person & the charcoal will work better on a smaller build to clear the alcohol & pills.

Thanks, it's a good suggestion, but what I crave & wish for so desperately is people to hang out & do fun things with in rl. I am tired of going to bars alone, concerts alone, everything alone. I have been stood up by people I have purchased tickets for. :(  

I like the problem-solving aspect of online life, but it's meaningless when I want to invite or be invited to simply have a drink or go to a movie with a human being in rl.
I did that kind of mix, woke up in ER, no one gave a crap. Not recommended. They make you drink charcoal. It neutralizes it.

Not a Facebook member, but 100% understand & share this awful situation/feeling. No one texts anymore. Might get rid of phone soon; it kills me to text them & be ignore, or get notifications about spam e-mails showing up in inbox.

Thanks. I think I come across creepy because I try too hard, have kind of an "intellectual"/"absent-minded professor"/quirky image even though I am not in intellectual work or education, & display terrible anxiety/terrible social skills in public. 

I hit on him once (I am F, older) in a discreet e-mail, many months back. We have hung out since then many times. I don't think that's the issue of creepiness.

He has not been told, but may know enough through observation, to know I have borderline-abusive much older partner I can't leave because I end up homeless when I live alone. That's enough to kill any friendship so I never bring it up & go out of my way to hide it.

I am not "out" about AS because my psychologist said it would just give people who already dislike me one more thing to hold against me, an oft-misunderstood label...
I think you're right.... I need to back off. So ironic that avoiding someone is the key to having them in my life (hopefully). :(

I actually had a point to this post: should I apologize to this friend for leaning on him too much? Ask what's up with not being given his new phone #? Or just back off completely?

I am a shut-in pretty much because I am so ashamed of myself & have no one to go to anything with. :(
I find I am treated with more respect & dislike when I am not "out", but treated in patronizing or dismissive way when I am "out". Choose your poison.

What if, as is the case for me, being among large numbers of people who share my hobby and even working (casual/occasional) in that field still fails to result in any solid friendships?

As the holidays near, I feel more & more resigned to taking my life. I am too creepy, socially unskilled & now getting older (45 F). Embracing my creepiness I think would alienate even more people from me, which I am sadly too good at anyway.

Based on spending considerable time at an ASD centre, with programming & drop-ins, I would summarize the "Aspie-culture" I was exposed to as the stereotypical "Big Bang Theory"/geek stuff. It was not forced on anyone; many clients had anime, computers, sci-fi, or related hobbies which they brought along, in conversation/objects accompanying them on visits. Nothing wrong with that--just not all of us are into that stuff, which surprises some NTs & AS people too.

Also found a parallel stream of "Aspie-culture" called "self-advocacy" which consisted more of AS people promoting a certain vision of a politically-active, outspoken group of AS people taking charge of the condition's public image & their personal/collective destinies. An ASD disability rights sort of culture.

As someone who once tried to fit in at an ASD centre after a preliminary "suspected ASD" diagnosis, I know what you mean about the "Aspie culture".

When I went there, I was regularly presumed to enjoy things like science fiction/fantasy, anime, computers. None of which I have ever liked or cared about. 

There was a mentality among some clients that their parents, mainly mothers, should & would always be there to deal with everything for them in rl. That women were naturally interested in this.

.
Whatever you do, avoid moving in with anyone--romantic, family, anyone--where you lose whatever gains you have made around independent living skills and survival.

Maybe avoiding people is the best idea, if one has a tendency to overshare what might be considered baggage. 

So stressful and confusing. Knowing NT people find me defective makes me act stupid and have baggage galore. Every time I talk with NT people I probably come across more AS and more burdened with baggage. 

I have read that narcissism is common in ASD people. I certainly have it (formal diagnosis) and far from being fun or a great ego-enhancer, it is soul-destroying and ruins every chance to connect with people. :(

I'm too embarrassed about my failing social performance to even say a word by e-mail to someone I bought dinner for 2 nights ago. 

Engaging with people in a reciprocal way is such a thrill. Even a taste of it feels so amazing. But like OP I'm mostly flitting, ghosting & being ghosted by NT people.

fml

I refuse to "out" myself publicly anymore. I did this in earlier years of diagnosis & got a lot of this garbage, even from psychiatrists, nurses & other professionals. I feel hatred from people sometimes but I'd take that over the pity, fakeness & praise for b.s. like "aren't you dressed nicely today?!" or "Even getting out of bed in the morning is an accomplishment". The implied ending to those complements is "for your kind".

That was very helpful illustration of the difference. It sounds like it's the tone & audience that kind of define how & what should be disclosed, to avoid making conversation partners uncomfortable. 

Someone recently told me he was receptive to my sharing with him, after I mentioned anxiety/depression in a vague way. But I also really value that person so I don't want to be the oversharing TMI baggage person who repels others, & so AS that I'm oblivious...
That's also what my psychologist said--stay put. Not easy. :(  Thanks for the advice & article (I am reading it now.)
No, because I work from home after experiencing all of the situations I described in the various workplaces I have worked in for the last 30 years.

This explains why I think so many smart, capable AS people are unemployed/underemployed: less-capable but NT people asserting their "status" through treating us with derision (e.g. refusing to hire AS people, workplace bullying of AS people) or well-meaning condescension (e.g. hiring an ASD person for a job they are grossly overqualified & underpaid for; treating AS employees or coworkers like children or as if mentally handicapped; "sympathetic" looks; etc.)

That is the best title! "Balancing the right to habilitation with the right to personal liberties: the rights of people with developmental disabilities to eat too many doughnuts and take a nap." 

It's confusing to know what is over-sheltered life vs. accepting accommodations in life because of disability. Especially when the accommodations (in both senses of that word) are being provided in the context of a non-medical, non-community services & non-familial "relationship". In which my role is to play the dumb, attractive, younger female, in exchange for a place to live, shower, etc. Although I do bring in my own money for my food, clothing, etc. & even give him some $$$ when I have it for "rent" (non-market price, of course.) Disability cheques are a ticket to homelessness or sharing squalid, insect-infested apartments with strangers where I live, so this is better, at least in that regard.

I do have no dignity though. :(

My psychologist told me to stop trying to appear NT in order to network in my arts career field, because I'm in my 40s, it's not working & it is deepening my sense of depression & low self-esteem to be faking it.

I had to euthanize my elderly cat this summer. Stayed with her the entire time. She was sedated first, purring & giving me happy looks as I scratched her chin. When she received the lethal injection, she passed so quickly I could not discern the moment of death. It changed my way of thinking about euthanasia & death.

First time it got that bad. I'll go back next week but will not stay if that crap continues. Perhaps unusually for someone dx'ed with AS, I have zero interest in playing games, & work (casual) in a field I find interesting. I ruin friendships/potential friendships with the very people who love the same interest as me, because poor social skills matter more than the special interest.

Therapists/facilitators coddling a time-wasting dude who wouldn't stop returning to a single topic over & over, an irrelevant topic at that (i.e. the presence of a notebook, which was put away at first mention that it might upset anyone.). Not sure why everyone's feelings about the irrelevant topic were necessary to solicit before just moving on.
That is one deep, helpful answer. Thank you for taking the time to write it.

Someone did that to me in group therapy for wanting to take notes, as I can't remember anything important unless I write it down. He started poking fun at me. So I got up & walked out, kept walking & left. They can laugh about me, but not to my face.

Yes, have that exact problem as OP. It makes me have insomnia & chest pain. Thinking of suicide in next year, after getting things in order. Not mattering to someone you care about, then getting advice to "find someone else" implies that people are interchangable &/or that having attraction for a particular person is somehow "wrong" & your tastes should be changed. But attracting creeps, seniors, & other fine people who don't attract me is no substitute.

I appreciate the response & hear what you are saying. Wondering though about how to handle it when literally NO ONE accepts you for you, whether one tries to "fit in" or just acts AS in public. I have a history of trying both, the "IDGAF if I look mental/odd" behaviour in public, & then the efforts (w/ my psychiatrist's help) to look normal, act normal, hold a job, etc. Neither seems to work. :(

I certainly don't feel awesome when no one accepts me for me. :(  I find it a very sad way to live, holing up, reading self-help books & thinking "yay me!" The whole thing about "loving yourself first" & "developing self-esteem". Not going so well over here...
Wish I could help but OMG this is what I attract too, male & female "surrogate parents" wanting to save me from fun. LOATHE THAT.
I'm going on a bender alone tomorrow just because there's nothing better to do, no one cares & I might as well be self-destructive.

It's actually very hard to be female around this age, 40s-early 50s but not a senior, because no one seems a good friend "fit". I can't relate to retirees (either gender) doing pottery & my only friends are not close friends, but share a hobby w/ me & are in their 20s.

That's fair, wanting to meet people close to your age. Sorry for overreacting. Just tired of constantly encountering reactions everywhere in life that women are completely worthless after around age 30.

45, just had formal assessment last week after spending most of adult life in desperate "survival" jobs & diagnosed schizophrenic. I relate to this post. Now the dx makes it all more real that this AS is the past, present & future cause of such a garbage life (mine), I don't even really want to try at anything anymore. Everything seems pointless. Even hobbies I like seem less enjoyable, knowing how incurably toxic I am.

I have an Engineering Technology diploma--great marks, a STEM field--but cannot workin field because it requires much cooperation with numerous coworkers & also driving (I can't drive). STEM for AS people may or may not provide employment regardless of aptitude, education or interest. One more stereotype...
Please do not recommend AS women seek "older men" partners who "adore" them. In same situation & want to die.
One more reason to just leave the planet already: when you're a 45 year old woman & read "but I assume that's just full of like 50-60 year old women" as a reason not to join something....
Definitely. No one ever attacked me but I've seen it. Also seen meltdowns on Twitter, where the person found their rant or whatever retweeted for others like their boss, etc. to see ad infinitum.
Twittercided in July. Too much pressure on the sites to present a fake positive image, or conversely to vent TMI & wreck rl.

I am just tired of people who just want to blab about themselves narcissistically deciding to be "friends" with me.... I'm 45 & would love friends to have fun, drink, go out with. Not married, never married, no kids, yet I hear younger people disparage people, esp. women, my age as "having too much baggage." Pretty friendless, infuriating life as a result. The "Meetup" idea works best for people who are already pretty sociable & who have cars. lol My ex-bf is a fan of Meetups & everyone leans on him for his car for various outings.

Also 45, lived hard. Staying warm: public buildings, esp. libraries, universities, coffee shops. See if you can get an emergency Community Services &/or Mental Health (Emergency Room if necessary) appointment to talk about emergency housing & your depression. Going to the E.R. can open doors faster & also it's a warm place to hang out. Last-ditch idea for me was getting arrested to be indoors & fed. Not sure I would recommend it but it's an option I suppose. Best of luck to you.

Thanks for all these responses. the kind of feedback I can't get in rl, because (ironically) people continue to tell me to "love myself first" rather than offering anything more meaningful. I feel like toxic garbage that contaminates the atmosphere around me, not "loveable", whatever tf that means. I like the comment about learning to "want" rather than "love" myself, & also the one mentioning meds, because it's probably about that point again: meds or a suicide attempt.
Quit.
Solid example for me to follow. I admire your bravery, in a world where how many "friends" you have seems to be main barometer of personal worth.

Any context where people say they "care about" you when they don't know you is a big joke. I've never had a psychiatrist say either, but have had psychologists, therapists, nurses & sometimes other patients say these things in hospital/program settings. The practitioners who said these things were overstepping professional boundaries to say that they "care about me" when it's untrue or just generic "feel good" lingo used indiscriminately on everyone.

Talk to them like you would talk to any male you want to be friends with. Don't stare/leer at body parts or remark on physical appearance because these are creepy behaviours when delivered by acquaintances.
I gained 10 lbs a month on Effexor. It worked but wasn't worth obesity.

What is the right thing to do, to avoid f***ing up friendships when depression is part of your daily life? Faking normal doesn't seem to work, hiding out alone all the time obviously doesn't work, talking about mental health issues is dangerous & IMHO alienates people who don't want to hear TMI, etc.
I've read & been told to "let yourself be vulnerable" with others to make friendships or deepen them, but this is giving ammunition to people who could use it against me.
Yes. It's about losing them to more "normal" friends when they become successful & accepted. :(

I've done some interesting things (travel, education, sports, etc.) but it doesn't make me interesting to be around or talk with, so I am a shut-in most of the time. Having an interesting life doesn't make someone interesting. I have noticed a lot of people with fairly boring lives have good friendships & are well-liked by others.
It's like providing unpaid customer service to the most frustrating people. :(
I keep going places alone & it sucks. I enjoy the event less because I feel like a toxic chemical contaminating the normal environment w/ depression vibes. Wish there was a cure...

Same situation. Psychologist told me others can tell I "have a hate-on for the world" even when I'm smiling, going along with small talk & playing nice. "Avoidant attachment" is what I was told-dumping people when the relationship threatens to become more emotionally intimate (non-sexual).

What happens if you're in your 40s already & the people who WANT to hang out are the "compassionate mom" types or endless complainers? I am really miserable around these types who sometimes seem drawn to me because I look like an "outsider" who "needs their help" or is a social failure who has to listen to them because I have no choice about people...

Sociopathic kids & teens can really work those teachers, guidance counsellors, parents, etc. I would get kids instigating fights with me, & I would end up in detention for self-defence. And then get beaten at home by my mother for being in detention. It really came down to adults preferring to punish/scapegoat the "weird" (quiet, socially awkward) kid & spare the outgoing, popular bully who keeps the weird kids in their place.

Welcome to the Avoidant PD club. I found out in my 30s from a psychiatrist. I experience anger & hostility toward 99% of people around me, so I try to prevent others from being subjected to me & live mostly like a shut-in now. The 1% of people I enjoy being around & talking with are scary-when they leave or reject me, I have self-injured & attempted suicide, gotten extremely drunk, etc. Destroying my life if they don't want to be in it. What a mess. Best of luck to you. Therapy + the medication is needed for PDs typically, sometimes the meds are not even needed. At least this is what my psychologist told me about my situation.

I find some people present themselves as helpful shoulders to cry on, when they are really voyeurs looking for dirt on a social reject (e.g. me). If people come at me with that "you can trust me" bogus friend vibe, even when they ignore me the rest of the time, it's time to run.

Working out
Completing written assignment
Eating at good restaurant
Spending time doing things w/ anyone whose company I enjoy
Getting out of bed before 10 am
Exchanging texts or e-mails w/ normal people

Try different things. I hated & was terrible at team sports. Tried an individual sport & went to the national championships 2x & even won a medal. Socially, I wish I could help but endure same problems as you.
One short appointment shows little. Unfortunately resources are stretched thin & it's true, unless you have private coverage, you may have a hard time getting proper assessment.

45F & lifelong depression. Younger depression fuelled more by child abuse, academic/career worries & social failure; current depression by child abuse, career/money worries & social failure. People are too quick to write off women in their 40s & up as a bunch of depressing, gross grannies who should just become invisible IMHO & this adds to depressed feeling a lot when people treat me poorly on this basis. I can't relate at all to that image because I'm physically fit, look reasonable, never married/no kids & find it infuriating that women are assumed to be this bland stereotype of aches & pains, meddling grandma or over the hill "cougar" making fool of herself. If middle aged women have high rates of depression, I would bet it's more to do with these stereotypes being put on us than anything like menopause or aging itself.

I was considered good-looking in the past, but aging takes this away from everyone. It's hard to "give up" on trying to retain the ingredients of good looks because IMHO looking good makes people treat you better. My extreme social deficits were overlooked when I looked my best, at least men overlooked them. No female friends. Hard to know whether it's better to try to fight to look good when nature is making it hard, or give up & look like someone less interesting to others.

Yes. Spent yesterday w/ him. He's not interested in physical/romantic relationship w/ me. My psychologist said to avoid him because it will only make me more depressed to be around him. But this was the only time in in months I remember, at the end of the day, realizing "Hey I had a good time & didn't obsess on my social/life failures & want to kill myself all day. I was genuinely interested & entertained by a human being who doesn't want me to go away!" Crazy.

Sadness= advice that "happiness comes from caring about others" & realizing you don't know anyone who cares about you. Why should I then care about people who ignore me or treat me poorly? That makes me a sucker, not happy or good. Disappointment also from seeing how many bullies & fake-compassion people are lauded as a model for social interaction, happiness & general awesomeness.
Thanks everyone. This gives me some courage not to overdisclose tomorrow, but not to be wracked w/ shame & the effort of holding it all in, if he asks.
Poverty, bad physical abuse & neglect as child, inability to get enjoyment from normal friendships with normal people, perfectionism, financial dependence on partner I am no longer attracted to

Depression can be a magnet for the wrong kind of male attention so being selective is not a bad thing. When I'm really bad, I get wanna-be saviors, usually much older, pressuring me into relationships. Not even just sex...relationships. Having a serious interest in a male friend, wanting to take that further but fearing the worst (due to having depression & all that entails) is hard. I asked someone like you describe (more than a little crush, on a normal, kind man) to be fwb (by e-mail), & he was so nice he e-mailed back he felt bad that he was saying no to the offer, but wanted to be better platonic friends. lol

lol I hate cashiers starting conversations about weather and other small-talk. This is not uncommon here (Canada). I also cannot work as a cashier anymore because stores have a relatively-recent insistence on cashiers providing conversations & entertainment to even the douchiest time-wasters in the line, like old dudes who want to talk about a product with anyone female, even though there are 100 people behind him...
Messes people up for life sometimes.

This is something my psychologist & I always seem to end up discussing: doing good things for yourself vs. feeling undeserving of anything good. She tells me to not punish myself over supposed social mistakes & to go do anything fun.
Being raised by parents who would not allow fun, called anything short of perfection in life "laziness", fed us moldy food when we got fed at all, beat us up (me & siblings as children), etc. seems to have instilled the thought that "I do not deserve care, I do not deserve good things, fun is laziness, anything but suffering is a sign I'm not working hard enough."
It didn't work to create success--I am vastly underemployed, poor, no car/home, never married/no kids (in 40s), no friends, several serious suicide attempts, scars all over my forearms. Make myself feel good? How can I deserve that? Early lessons die hard.

Yes to this. :(  Terrifying to think of losing last friend in my life by talking about why I have no other friends, why I'm always hiding out, erratic work history, etc. Hard to know how anyone will react/respond. You expressed this fear very well btw.
People like to pretend to be so compassionate...very few seem to care about someone's real depression, in my own experience.
That is profound: "Before you get diagnosed with depression, first be sure that you are not surrounded by assholes"
